problem: f:two-to-one includes "possibly a re-poll to see if opinions have improved" in the norm itself, so re-polling on a count above 2:1 does not depart from it.
fix: Cut "or re-polling", so that only declining departs.

problem: The norm as f:two-to-one and d:positions state it says what normally happens above 2:1 and gives no call at or below, so declaring consensus there departs from nothing it says, and p:deadlock itself lists "a chair calls consensus below the norm". l:call-below, l:dchair-call, l:norm-forwarding, and the second sentence of p:cutoff-effect inherit this.
fix: Add a cited premise that under SD-4 a proposal at or below 2:1 normally does not advance.

problem: f:present-required and f:invested let another presenter pass feedback to an author who revises, so a record of responding to review can come from revisions without taking part; l:review-needs-part gives SD-4's expectation, not exclusivity.
fix: Weaker wording: "SD-4 expects that record to come from taking part."

problem: f:plenary-weight says such objections "should not be given weight", which is SD-4's instruction, not what happens; p:plenary-ratifies and inf:nb-late-plenary repeat "get no weight".
fix: Weaker wording: "SD-4 says should get no weight there."

problem: "national bodies, which form positions only where that is worth their members' time" needs a national body to count its members' time as a cost, but ax:prefer lists a national body's values as outcomes and national interests, and l:nb-position-time shows only that positions take that time. inf:nb-cost, inf:nm-more, and inf:nl-fewer inherit it.
fix: Add a cited premise, or weaker wording: "national bodies, whose positions take their members' time".

problem: d:result-seeking ties a result-seeking author's gain to how well the adopted design serves users, which a flaw found later lowers, so "An author gains at adoption" does not cover all of an author's gain; inf:thm-reward-timing and l:thm-costs-gains repeat it.
fix: Weaker wording: "An author's gain from adoption itself comes at adoption."

problem: A vote can also reflect the design that serves users best when the voter's other values point the same way, so "weighs a good result for users above other values" is stronger than ax:prefer supports. p:merit-gap, inf:thm-merit-gap, and l:thm-merit inherit it.
fix: Weaker wording: "and no other value outweighs it".

problem: "No rule requires a written answer" goes beyond f:no-paper-objections and f:respond-comments, which cover SD-4 and the named ISO clauses only.
fix: Weaker wording: "Neither SD-4 nor the searched ISO clauses require a written answer".

problem: "A written answer to an objection states the objection it answers" rests only on ax:turnover, which says a clear written objection is easier to raise again but does not supply that an answer states the objection clearly.
fix: Weaker wording: "A written answer that states the objection clearly makes it easier to raise again."

problem: ax:schedule says WG21 plans an edition every three years and d:edition defines the cutoff, but neither says an edition goes ahead on schedule without the features that miss it, so "keeps an unfinished feature from delaying the features that are ready" is unsupported; inf:deadlock-schedule inherits it.
fix: Add a cited premise, or cut the clause.

problem: f:incits-caucus lets the United States delegation determine the official United States position on a new issue, not decide the issue.
fix: Weaker wording: "may also determine the United States position on a new issue at an international plenary by caucus consensus".

problem: ax:support speaks of Against, Neutral, and not voting and says nothing about Favor, so no cited item supplies that a Favor vote gives the colleague no reason to support the voter less readily. inf:favor-cost, l:favor-supported, l:doubt-options, and thm:settled ("Favor risks nothing with the colleague") rest on it.
fix: Add a cited premise, for example a clause in ax:support.

problem: "propose first the smallest part that fixes the features its gain depends on" drops the condition in p:first-part that the part "still meets the 2:1 norm against opponents who foresee the rest"; thm:settled, inf:pa-design-bound, and inf:fp-small repeat it.
fix: Restore the condition.

problem: inf:omit-free shows only that leaving a trade-off out costs nothing "the rules impose", but the lemma needs it to cost nothing at all, for example no loss of standing if implementation later exposes it (ax:unknown).
fix: Add a cited premise, or weaker wording: "does no better, counting only the costs the rules impose".

problem: When objectors who can keep the norm unmet ask only for changes to the features the author's gain depends on, the cheapest change that keeps the norm met changes those features with no room direction, so "leaves the features ... alone unless the room directs a change to them" is too strong.
fix: Weaker wording: "unless the room directs a change to them or only such a change keeps the norm met".

problem: "When those costs, which grow with each meeting it waits ..., outweigh it" counts meetings already paid for, which stopping cannot recover, while l:small-keep-stop compares the chance of adoption with the costs still to come; inf:sf-small repeats the step.
fix: Weaker wording: "When the cost of the meetings still ahead outweighs its chance of adoption".

problem: It applies p:chair-threshold, which concerns departing from the 2:1 norm, to departing from a polling order SD-4 only encourages, and nothing cited links that to a chair's post.
fix: Add a cited premise, or cut the post clause.

problem: f:plenary-weight gives unescalated objections no weight and f:plenary-consent defines unanimous consent over all positions, but no cited item says the convenor then declares consensus; inf:nm-unsettled builds on it.
fix: Weaker wording: "SD-4's plenary procedure gives that opposition no weight in the convenor's consensus call."

problem: d:sponsor says a sponsor pays some or all of a participant's costs, not that every participant has one, and a user who takes part becomes a participant a sponsor could pay, so "bears the full price of attending alone" does not follow. l:user-take-part, l:settled-user, and thm:settled inherit it.
fix: Weaker wording: "a user with no sponsor bears the full price".

problem: No item shows that any listed rule acts on any effect the proof derives, and p:integration says the editing committee verifies only that changes were applied, not that designs work together; l:thm-checks-sizes and thm:settled go further with "checks on each of these effects".
fix: Weaker wording: "The rules also contain these provisions."

problem: The settled lemmas compare each named choice with only some of the moves m:moves lists, not, for example, a regular's attending, studying, writing a paper, or private concern, or a chair's time-boxing or one-meeting delay, so "at least as well ... as any other move the rules give it" does not follow.
fix: Weaker wording: "as any alternative the settled lemmas consider", or add lemmas for the remaining moves.

problem: The basis shows a design can become the incumbent when least reviewed, after which changes bear a growing cost, while l:rival-with-paper and f:direction-implement show the room can still direct changes, so "content can be fixed" is too strong; the chapter's closing summary repeats it.
fix: Weaker wording: "a design can become the incumbent when it is least reviewed".

problem: "review whose gain is spread across all users goes undone" drops the condition in p:review-shortfall that the review is worth less to any one participant than its cost, and every design's gain is spread across its users (ax:users-affected).
fix: Restore the condition.

problem: ax:first-review says reviewers cannot study "in detail" what later parts require until those parts are presented, and l:first-part-foresight lets those who foresee the rest vote on it, so "before anyone can study" is too strong.
fix: Weaker wording: "before reviewers can study in detail".

problem: No cited item makes room attendance available, and f:protected keeps meeting records protected apart from poll questions and numeric results, so "attendance gives the number present" is unsupported.
fix: Add a cited source for attendance, or measure abstention another way.

problem: The model predicts splitting only for design-bound authors (inf:pa-design-bound) or where sooner adoption outweighs a paper and presentation per part (p:parts, l:settled-result-seeking), so a large design adopted in one paper fits the model and should not count against it.
fix: Weaker wording: "large proposals with design-bound authors appear as sequences of papers", with matching counter-evidence.

problem: No settled-pattern lemma concerns how authors title papers or how chairs word polls, and the reversal cost bears on what voters value, not on wording.
fix: Add a cited premise linking wording to the reversal cost, or restate the prediction as less support for rivals.

problem: The innocent explanation concerns wording and accepts the same real reversal cost after incumbency (ind:reversal-grows), so it also predicts less support for a like rival afterward, and "the same support" does not follow.
fix: Compare how like rivals are worded before and after incumbency instead of their support.

problem: Under f:plenary-reason a chair answers only when a participant asks, so no answer at plenary can mean no one asked, which neither explanation addresses.
fix: Cut "and their absence favors the model", or limit the comparison to objections someone raised at plenary.

problem: Unanimous consent is a plenary outcome (f:plenary-consent), and a feature can pass plenary that way after Against votes in a subgroup, so the two compared groups overlap.
fix: Define both groups at the same poll, for example subgroup forwarding polls with and without Against votes.

problem: l:settled-convenor gives opposition that holds no national position as one case where the procedure has the convenor declare consensus, not the only one, and no cited item bars a call over opposition that holds a national position.
fix: Weaker wording: "the room's count need not settle opposition that holds one".

problem: SD-4's direction group charter includes "Providing an opinion on any specific proposal: This includes whether the proposal should be pursued or not, and if pursued any changes that should be considered," and design rooms are "strongly encouraged to give weight" to it, while the design rooms "own selecting and recommending feature designs." So SD-4 does give bodies the job of judging proposals. What it lacks is anyone who rules for the room. As written, the Fact and p:who-decides ("SD-4 assigns no one to judge a design's quality") are false.
fix: Narrow the Fact and p:who-decides to "SD-4 gives no one the power to rule on a design's quality for the rooms," and name the direction group's opinion, which design rooms are encouraged to weigh, beside it.

problem: "only Against voters can be asked for reasons" turns an absence (f:no-reasons-other: SD-4 names no such step for other voters) into a bar. Nothing in SD-4 stops a chair, who runs discussion and "may take any polls they choose," from asking a Neutral or Favor voter why they voted that way. What only Against voters have is SD-4's request that they "be prepared to articulate their rationale." This matters later: c:lever-reasons-all treats "a chair could ask voters of every position" as a change from today, when it may already be allowed.
fix: Write "only Against voters are told by SD-4 to be prepared to give reasons, which takes time," and restate c:lever-reasons-all as SD-4 telling voters of every position to be prepared to give reasons.

problem: The definition also requires "a process that involves seeking to take into account the views of all parties concerned and to reconcile any conflicting arguments." Reconciling conflicting arguments means dealing with what they say. The lemma replaces that with the weaker "every view must still be heard," so l:call-from-votes, l:thm-merit, and the Theorem read as if the test ignores what an objection argues.
fix: Replace "and every view must still be heard" with "though the process must seek to take every view into account and to reconcile conflicting arguments," and carry that clause into inf:test-not-right and inf:thm-merit-no-judge.

problem: "Finding out whether those objectors are right leaves that count unchanged" is false. What participants learn can change their votes (ax:attention), and the 2:1 norm applies "after discussion of the concerns of those voting against and possibly a re-poll to see if opinions have improved." That re-poll is exactly where finding out moves the count. l:study-count shows only that studying takes time and that the comparison counts votes.
fix: Write "Finding out whether those objectors are right changes that count only through the votes it moves at a re-poll."

problem: A direction poll approves only "whether to continue work on a design" (d:polls), and SD-4 expects the author to "implement any changes directed by the group, typically for subsequent revisions." A later directed change carries that approval out. It does not remove or replace it, so under d:reversal the clause "or later changing it" names no reversal. That clause is the only support for "every later change to it bears a reversal cost" in p:early-polls, l:bound-early, l:seeking-early, inf:thm-early-cost, and the Theorem.
fix: Drop "or later changing it" and the claims that rest on it, or define what a direction poll approves to include the design's content as polled and state that a directed change reverses that.

problem: Under d:incumbent, two designs on one topic can both pass direction polls, which SD-4's encouragement to poll alternatives side by side makes likely. Each is then an incumbent, and keeping one replaces the other. In that case "Keeping an incumbent removes or replaces nothing" is false, and so is p:challenger-bar's "which faces no such hurdle itself."
fix: Restrict both items to a rival that has not passed a direction poll on the topic, or define the incumbent as the only design on its topic that has passed one.

problem: SD-4's line for voting is being "familiar with the material," meaning having read the paper and paid close attention to the discussion. That costs far less than the close study p:review-share prices, and the presentation exists "to educate a group of general C++ experts." A participant who reads a long paper and follows its presentation without studying it closely typically votes. So "voted on mainly by those with large stakes" does not follow from p:review-share, and the Theorem's light-review sentence and c:pred-abstention-length inherit the gap.
fix: Rest p:light-review on the cost of reading the paper and following its discussion, and show that this cost grows with size. Otherwise limit the result to proposals whose material most participants do not read.

problem: The ranking lemmas need departing from the norm to put a chair's post at more risk than following it, but this sentence gives only that departing "can" cost the post. No rule or axiom ties a chair's post to their consensus calls, and m:players takes the convenor's appointments as given. Following the norm can equally cost a post. So l:call-above, l:call-below, inf:sg-order-cost, l:settled-sg-chair, l:settled-design-chair, and the Theorem's chair sentence rest on an unstated premise.
fix: Add an axiom that a chair's post is at more risk from a call that departs from SD-4's stated practice than from one that follows it, and cite it in place of "can cost."

problem: SD-4 puts the re-poll inside the norm itself ("after discussion of the concerns of those voting against and possibly a re-poll to see if opinions have improved"), and "The subgroup chair may take any polls they choose." So a re-poll departs from nothing at any count. Yet l:call-above, inf:call-above-norm, and t:chair-call count re-polling as a departure above the line, the same as declining.
fix: Above the line, rank declaring consensus only against declining. Treat a re-poll as within the norm at every count.

problem: SD-4 adopts ISO's definition (p:definition-without-procedure), under which consensus is the absence of sustained opposition by an important part of the concerned interests. It also says the majority "cannot just say 'we have enough votes' and refuse to listen." A chair who finds such opposition above 2:1 follows SD-4 by declining, so inf:call-above-norm's "departs from it" is false in that case. The mirror case is a chair who finds consensus at or below the line because the opposition comes from no important part, which l:call-below treats as a departure. So the count alone does not fix "the call the norm gives."
fix: Add to both lemmas and to t:chair-call the condition "and the chair's judgment of sustained opposition agrees with the count."

problem: Check not stated: the sentence in SD-4 that allows the delay begins "we do not significantly delay progress on concrete proposals in order to wait for alternative proposals we might get in the future." At the feature cutoff, a one-meeting delay costs a full edition, three years, which is significant by any reading. So SD-4's own principle weighs against using the delay there. That bears on l:settled-design-chair, which cites this item.
fix: Add "though SD-4 says it does not significantly delay concrete proposals to wait for alternatives" to the first sentence, and put f:no-wait-alternatives in its basis.

problem: The lemma's children show only that a design can become the incumbent when it is least reviewed and that rivals then face a growing reversal cost. Nothing shows the content is fixed. SD-4 expects the room to direct changes after a direction poll and the author to make them, so the content keeps changing. "a design's content can be fixed when it is least reviewed" is unsupported, and it is the Theorem's headline.
fix: Write "a design can become the incumbent when it is least reviewed" here, in the Theorem, and in ch 11's plain terms.

problem: "review whose gain is spread across all users goes undone" drops the condition that inf:thm-review-undone keeps ("but less to any one participant"). It also conflicts with inf:co-stake, which says close study of a rival is worth more to a competing author than to most participants, so in the pattern some such review does get done.
fix: Write "review worth more to users together than to any one participant who could do it goes undone," here and in the Theorem.

problem: The evidence needs the number present when each poll was taken. SD-4 lets only "straw poll questions and numeric results" be quoted from meeting records, so who was in the room for a poll sits in protected material. The share not voting cannot be computed from what the corollary names.
fix: Name the source of the number present, such as protected minutes used with permission, or replace the share not voting with a measure built only from quotable numeric results.

problem: After a direction poll, the room has given the incumbent more review time, and what it learned can lower support for a like rival even when no reversal cost is involved (ax:attention). The before-and-after comparison cannot tell incumbency from learning.
fix: Compare like rivals before and after incumbency only where the room spent no further review time on the incumbent between the two polls, or hold review time fixed.

problem: To show that a paper "leaves unstated the objections" it faced, one needs the list of objections raised, including the reasons Against voters gave when asked. That list sits in meeting records SD-4 keeps password-protected. Papers and poll results show which polls had Against votes, not which objections were raised, so they cannot test the prediction.
fix: Name as evidence the protected records of the objections raised, used under SD-4's consent rule, or limit the prediction to objections stated in published papers.

problem: The Theorem says "no player improves their position by changing only their own choice," but m:players takes the convenor's appointments, study groups, and guest invitations as given, and no lemma shows they are best responses. The chairs' post risk in p:chair-threshold is a threat carried out through those appointment choices. Since the proof never shows that replacing a departing chair is the convenor's best response, it never shows that the threat holds in the pattern.
fix: Write "no player improves their position by changing only a choice the proof does not take as given," or add a lemma showing that replacing a chair who departs from SD-4's practice is a best response for the convenor.

problem: SD-4's header names the convenor as its reply-to, and the convenor maintains SD-4 and can revise its plenary procedure. m:moves-convenor leaves that move out. "follow SD-4's plenary procedure unless their stake is worth more than what departing can cost them" treats as fixed a text that one of the players can change.
fix: Add to m:players that the proof takes SD-4's text as given, including any revision the convenor could make, and limit the Theorem's convenor sentence to that case.

problem: SD-4's plenary procedure fixes the convenor's call in only two cases: no objection to unanimous consent, and opposition that is all unescalated and holds no national position. For opposition escalated in time, whether personal or national, SD-4 says only that the convenor "will usually ask" which it is and that plenary decides "whether there is consensus, as determined by the Convener." So "follow SD-4's plenary procedure" names no choice in the cases that matter most, and the Theorem's convenor sentence is incomplete there.
fix: State that SD-4's procedure fixes the convenor's call only in those two cases, and that the proof takes the convenor's call as given when opposition was escalated in time.

problem: "SD-4's plenary procedure has the convenor declare consensus over opposition only when it holds no national position" turns l:convenor-weightless around. That lemma gives a condition under which the convenor declares consensus, not the only one. SD-4 states no effect of a national position on the convenor's call, and ISO has experts "act in a personal capacity" and the convenor act "in a purely international capacity." So "the room's count does not settle opposition that holds one" is unsupported, and both c:lever-nb-more and c:lever-nb-less (through inf:nl-count) rest on it.
fix: Write "SD-4's plenary procedure fixes the convenor's call over opposition only when it holds no national position, and states no effect of a national position," and state as a premise of both levers that a national position weighs more at plenary than a personal one.

problem: By d:positions, the 2:1 norm is "SD-4's statement on subgroup polls." The convenor's plenary call follows the unanimous-consent and 3-way poll procedure, not a ratio. So "Departing from the 2:1 norm can cost the caller's post: ... the convenor for terms SC22 may decline to renew" names a norm the convenor does not apply, yet l:convenor-depart and l:settled-convenor cite this item for the convenor's cost.
fix: Write "Departing from SD-4's practice for the call can cost the caller's post."

problem: "since it needs a consensus call, which the 2:1 norm normally supports" is stated for "rooms and plenary." At plenary, SD-4 sets no ratio, and the convenor determines consensus after asking about unanimous consent and, when someone objects, taking a 3-way poll.
fix: Write "since it needs consensus calls, which in subgroups the 2:1 norm normally supports and at plenary the convenor makes."

problem: The proposition is unconditional, while l:iso-register-level leaves open whether ISO's sustained-opposition steps apply inside a working group. Clause 2.5.7 defines sustained oppositions as "views expressed at minuted meetings of the committee, working group (WG) or other groups." On the reading that its steps reach those meetings, the leadership "will register the opposition (i.e. in the report/minutes, records, etc.)" when it judges a declared opposition not sustained, or sustained but not resolvable. In those cases the record must show an objection that was outvoted, not answered.
fix: Add "unless an objector declares a sustained opposition and ISO's registration step applies within the working group, which ISO does not say," and carry the condition into inf:thm-record and the Theorem.

problem: False as stated. SD-4's TS paragraph says a TS, "when technically complete is sent by WG21 to be formally balloted with a round of formal review comments collated by ISO that must be formally responded to with a Disposition of Comments paper." That rule requires a written answer to each such comment, and the proposition's exceptions leave it out. ISO 2.5.6 also has successive committee drafts considered with a focus on "resolving the comments raised by National Bodies."
fix: Add "and the Disposition of Comments SD-4 requires for TS ballot comments" to the exceptions, with a Fact quoting it, and bring l:paper-answers in line.

problem: inf:no-gains-nothing says "its comments gain nothing from a No," but f:respond-comments quotes "Every attempt shall be made to resolve negative votes," which gives a No a resolution effort that comments with a Yes do not get. Also, one body's No lowers approval's chance only when it can change the result, and the two-thirds and one-quarter rules make that rare. That is the same pivot reasoning p:objector-coordination applies to Against votes. A body that values the rest and expects approval either way can do better voting No. p:nb-comment, t:nb-ballot, p:credible-threat, l:settled-nb, and the Theorem's national body sentence all inherit the gap.
fix: Limit the ranking to a body whose No could change the ballot's result, and add ISO's effort to resolve negative votes as a gain from No that the body weighs.

problem: The first sentence covers papers approved at one meeting, but l:thm-gaps and the Theorem say "separately adopted designs." For designs adopted at different meetings, the later paper's wording "is written against these adopted drafts," which already hold the earlier design. The wording room forwards it only when its specification "correctly expresses the intended design," and it refers design questions back to the design room. That is a step where a later design meets earlier ones, and p:checks leaves it out.
fix: Limit the Theorem's clause to "designs approved at the same meeting," or add to p:checks the wording rooms' review against the adopted drafts as a check across meetings.

problem: "Objections count only in the forms and times that attending teaches" does not fit where those rules live. SD-4 writes the forms and times down: escalation by 5pm on the email lists and within the national body, and ballot comments that bring new information. It also says "everyone who participates in WG21 is expected to be familiar with this information." ax:learning says some procedure is learned only by attending, but nothing shows the objection rules are among it.
fix: Write "Objections count only in fixed forms and times, which SD-4 states and attending also teaches," here and in the Theorem.

problem: Most defect reports concern wording, which SD-4 sends to issues lists with no design change. So "The model predicts rare removals even where such reports are many" holds under the innocent explanation too, and the comparison does not tell the two apart.
fix: Compare removals with reports or papers that ask for an adopted design to be removed or replaced.

problem: At plenary "Most polls pass by unanimous consent," including polls on features that drew Against votes in subgroups, because objections not escalated in time get no weight there. inf:de-predict classifies features by the adopting poll, which puts contested features in the unanimous group and blurs the comparison.
fix: Classify features by whether Against votes remained at the design room's forwarding poll, not by the plenary poll that adopted them.

problem: Whether an Against vote at plenary was a national position is recorded in the plenary minutes. SD-4 keeps meeting records protected, and the answer to the convenor's question about national positions is neither a straw poll question nor a numeric result. Of the evidence named, only the ballot comments are public.
fix: Name as evidence the protected plenary minutes, used under SD-4's consent rule, or rest the prediction on ballot comments alone.

problem: Check not stated: INCITS 7.17.1.3 says "All official U.S. positions shall be supported by all U.S. delegates," and that the TAG "may determine official US positions on Plenary meeting agenda items in advance of the meeting, and the delegation shall abide by those positions." Once a United States position exists, every United States delegate must support it, whoever pays them. That limits the weight a sponsor's paid participants can add, which p:nb-members leaves open.
fix: Add a Fact quoting 7.17.1.3, and add a clause to l:incits-votes and p:nb-members that United States delegates must support an official position once it is set.

problem: Check not stated: INCITS 3.9.2.4 says "For membership on the Executive Board, a business entity will not be considered separate if it is under the Control of another business entity." The Executive Board approves the United States position (f:incits-position), so a sponsor cannot multiply its votes there through companies it controls.
fix: Add a Fact quoting the control rule and a matching clause in l:incits-votes.

problem: Under ax:rework, a reversal's cost falls on whoever built on the design, mainly its authors, implementers, and wording reviewers. Most voters built nothing, so their share can stay near zero however much is built. For them, "That hurdle grows with each decision built on the incumbent" is unsupported, yet inf:thm-incumbent-edge and inf:rp-tell-apart rely on it for every voter.
fix: Write "That hurdle grows with each decision built on the incumbent for a voter who bears part of the work built on it."

problem: "each later part builds on the parts already adopted" follows neither from m:moves-author nor from ax:rework, which says only that later proposals can depend on a design. The parts of a large design can be separable, and a later part may rely on no earlier one. Yet ind:adopted-parts, p:parts, p:first-part, and c:pred-parts assume dependence throughout.
fix: Write "each later part that depends on adopted parts builds on them," and restrict ind:adopted-parts and the items that rest on it to designs whose later parts depend on the earlier ones.

problem: "The cost is a paper and a presentation for each part" is incomplete. Each part must pass its own polls in the design room, the wording room, and plenary, and l:first-part-oppose has opponents who foresee the rest vote against it early. Each extra meeting also costs attendance (ax:cost). A design in parts therefore faces more chances to be stopped. That changes whether presenting in parts does better than one paper, which p:first-part and l:settled-design-bound take as settled.
fix: Write "The cost includes a paper, a presentation, and a set of polls for each part," and add to p:first-part a comparison of parts with a single paper.

problem: "Each step it advances brings it nearer to work that can make plenary progress" holds for every proposal. SD-4's category is "work that can make plenary progress at this meeting," which a small proposal reviewed within one meeting enters sooner than a large one whose review spans editions. The sentence implies an edge for large proposals that the priority rule, if anything, gives to small ones, and inf:sf-predict in c:pred-small-fade relies on it.
fix: Drop the second sentence, or state that a small proposal can enter the plenary-progress category sooner than a large one, and remove the clause from inf:sf-predict.

problem: The proposition leaves out what a TS gives a design-bound author. SD-4 says a TS lets the committee publish "even when there is not yet consensus on the design, when people and national bodies typically still have strong technical concerns but are temporarily willing to publish without making the changes suggested by those concerns." At merge, "the default action ... is to move forward with the proposal we have," and people are "encouraged not to rehash decisions that already had consensus when the TS or white paper was started." Where the IS cannot reach consensus, a TS ships the features the author needs and favors them at merge. So "seek the IS over a TS" in l:settled-design-bound and the Theorem holds only where the IS is within reach.
fix: Add a Fact quoting the "temporarily willing to publish" sentence, and limit the design-bound author's preference to cases where the IS can reach consensus by the same cutoff.

problem: inf:omit-free shows only that leaving a trade-off out costs nothing "the rules impose." A drawback no reviewer raises can still come out through implementation and use (ax:unknown), and then an author who knew of it and left it out can lose standing, which ax:prefer counts. A large proposal faces polls across more than one edition, so standing matters most to its authors. "does no better than to leave out" is therefore unsupported.
fix: Add the condition "and whose later discovery would cost the author no standing," and carry it into l:settled-design-bound and the Theorem.

problem: The cheapest change that keeps the 2:1 norm met in the design room ignores later checks the proof itself names. An objector can raise the matter within their national body (l:objection-to-nb), which can take a national position at plenary, comment, and vote on the ballot. A design-bound author whose features must last to publication does not do best with a change that only keeps the room's count.
fix: Write "the cheapest change that keeps the 2:1 norm met and leaves no objection a national body would take up at plenary or ballot," and match the Theorem.

problem: "An author gains at adoption" leaves out what the author loses later. Every participant values "a good result for users" (ax:prefer). A sponsored author whose sponsor implements and ships the feature also bears its flaws through the sponsor's interests, and can lose standing. The Theorem's "An author gains at adoption, while a hidden flaw costs users later" implies the author escapes that cost.
fix: Write "An author gains in part at adoption, while a flaw that implementation and use have not yet exposed costs users, and in part the author, only after adoption," and match the Theorem.

problem: "reviewed before anyone can study what the later parts need of it" is false when the author publishes or describes the later parts. It also contradicts l:first-part-foresight, under which those who foresee the rest can base their vote on what the later parts need. ax:first-review says only that reviewers cannot study the later parts "in detail" until they are presented.
fix: Write "reviewed before the later parts are presented, so reviewers can study what those parts need of it only as far as the author or their own foresight describes them."

problem: "every rival must then replace it," which also appears in p:first-part, holds only for a rival to the structure the first part fixes. A rival to a later part that keeps the adopted first part replaces nothing in it.
fix: Write "every rival to the structure it fixes must then replace it" here, in p:first-part, and in the Theorem.

problem: SD-4 asks a good paper to "Show design alternatives considered: along with concrete examples showing why they were not pursued." Showing why an alternative lost to the chosen design means stating what each does better, which is a trade-off in substance even though SD-4 never uses the word. The Theorem's "The rules ask no author to state a trade-off" claims more than f:no-drawbacks-asked found.
fix: Write "The rules ask no author to state their own design's drawbacks, beyond showing why the alternatives considered were not pursued," here, in l:thm-disclosure, and in the Theorem.

problem: The tell-apart test compares the same participants' votes on "proposals of similar design on the same topic from authors with other affiliations." On the same topic, such a proposal is a rival to the sponsor's proposal. The proof's own reversal cost (p:challenger-bar) predicts fewer Favor votes for it from anyone already backing the incumbent, whoever pays them. The comparison therefore mixes sponsorship with incumbency.
fix: Compare proposals of similar design on different topics, or on the same topic only before either design has passed a direction poll.

problem: The test needs individual votes ("comparing their votes with their votes"). SD-4 allows quoting only poll questions, numeric results, and words or positions attributed to a person "with that person's prior consent." The named evidence, poll results and stated affiliations, cannot supply individual votes.
fix: Restate the test in terms of each poll's Against share, or name consented attributions of positions as the evidence.

problem: SD-4 expects the author to "implement any changes directed by the group, typically for subsequent revisions," so a later part written before the room has finished changing the earlier one soon goes out of date. Publishing each part only after the last is adopted also follows from the review process, so the timing test does not tell the two apart. For the same reason, inf:pa-ease's "reviewing in parts is as easy when the parts are published together" is unsupported.
fix: Use a test the directed-change process does not produce, such as whether drafts or implementations of the later parts existed when the first part was polled.

problem: When later parts are designed after the first is adopted, they rely on its choices because they are built on it, not because anything was left out. Under step-by-step design, "later parts relied on choices in the first that it did not describe" is expected too, so it does not favor the model.
fix: Require evidence that the later parts existed, in drafts, implementations, or talks, when the first paper was presented.

problem: The list leaves out that a sponsor can itself vote where a national position is formed: INCITS counts corporations as organizations with one voting membership each (f:incits-organization, f:incits-one-vote). l:settled-sponsor and l:thm-pattern therefore test the sponsor's choice against an incomplete set of moves.
fix: Add "and, where a national body's rules allow, vote as a member organization where its position is formed, as INCITS counts each organization once", and weigh that move in l:settled-sponsor.

problem: f:no-reasons-other supports only that SD-4 names no step for asking other voters. Nothing in SD-4 stops a chair, who "may take any polls they choose" (f:chair-polls), from asking a Favor or Neutral voter why, so "only Against voters can be asked for reasons" overstates the rule, and p:prefer-vs-stop and c:lever-reasons-all rest on it.
fix: "only Against voters are told by SD-4 that the chair may ask their reasons and that they should be prepared to give them"

problem: A regular who would otherwise vote Favor can put a doubt into the count by voting Neutral or not voting, which leaves one fewer Favor vote and draws no request for reasons. The doubt then reaches the 2:1 count with no Against vote, so "enters the 2:1 count only if" is false.
fix: "A regular's doubt about a colleague's proposal adds to the Against side of the 2:1 count only if it is worth the extra cost of an Against vote."

problem: A sponsor adds a voter only when its payment is what brings the participant to the room. An expert who would attend anyway, at their own cost or another sponsor's, adds no voter when this sponsor pays, yet l:settled-sponsor, c:pred-sponsor-against, and c:lever-sponsor-limit count every paid participant as an added voter.
fix: "A sponsor adds a voter to a room for each participant it pays who would not otherwise attend."

problem: Every proposal comes nearer to work that can make plenary progress as it advances, and a small proposal, whose author expects its design review within one meeting (d:small), can be such work at its first meeting. The last sentence gives large proposals no edge over small ones, yet inf:sf-predict relies on it to explain why small proposals stop advancing more often.
fix: Drop the last sentence, or state it of every proposal and remove it from inf:sf-predict's basis.

problem: SD-4 gives a study group the job of producing an initial proposal (f:sg-initial-proposal) but does not require every rival design on its topic to be polled there first, and the same sentence goes on to say the design room can poll a rival that has a paper. p:sg-sponsor and the Theorem's "study groups included" rest on the study group choosing among all the rivals.
fix: "rival designs can first be polled there"

problem: A third of the Favor-plus-Against votes keeps the 2:1 norm unmet (l:vote-count), but "enough to block" assumes the study group chair sends on only designs that meet it, which f:two-to-one does not require, since it says only when a proposal normally advances. p:checks uses "block" the same way.
fix: "enough to keep the 2:1 norm unmet", here and in p:checks.

problem: SD-4 lists approval polls among those a chair may take, in which the chair "takes a single show of hands for those 'not opposed' to each alternative" and "Typically there is then a runoff approval poll among the most popular options" (SD-4, "Subgroup responsibility and polls", not quoted in the proof), though it says they are typically used for naming. That lets a chair find which deadlocked design draws less opposition without the 2:1 comparison, a check on how long a deadlock lasts that this sentence and p:attrition leave out.
fix: Quote the approval poll and add "or a chair finds by approval poll which design draws less opposition" to the ways a deadlock ends.

problem: The sponsor, a player in m:players, bears the cost its participants are spared, and l:settled-sponsor has it keep paying only while the votes they add are worth that cost to it. Whether a sponsored group can hold through a long deadlock therefore turns on the sponsor's stake and cost as well as the members', and neither this sentence, t:hold-or-yield, nor the Theorem's "can hold longest" includes the sponsor's choice.
fix: State it of "a group whose sponsors keep paying its costs", and add to the table caption that each sponsor values its participants' holding above what it pays.

problem: In a side-by-side poll of rival designs (f:multiple-polls), a Favor vote for one design is a vote for it over a colleague's rival, and nothing in the axioms rules out that the rival's author then supports the voter less readily. inf:favor-cost's "no other vote costs the regular less" is shown only for standing with the proposal's own author.
fix: "Favor costs the regular no standing with the proposal's author and no time for reasons", here and in inf:favor-cost.

problem: SD-4's conduct slide asks everyone to "Act in good faith & with due care & diligence" (f:good-faith), and an omitted trade-off found later is new information, which SD-4 accepts as grounds to raise a decided matter again on the email lists or in a ballot comment (f:late-info, f:ballot-new-info). Leaving it out therefore carries risks the rules impose, so inf:omit-free's "costs the author nothing the rules impose" and the Theorem's matching sentence go too far.
fix: "Leaving it out costs the author no step the rules require before adoption", here, in inf:omit-free, and in the Theorem.

problem: "The rules ask no author to state a trade-off" is broader than its support. SD-4 asks a good paper to show the design alternatives considered "along with concrete examples showing why they were not pursued" (f:show-alternatives), which asks for the trade-offs between the design and each alternative; f:no-drawbacks-asked supports only that no paper is asked to state its own design's drawbacks.
fix: "The rules ask no author to state their own design's drawbacks", here and in l:thm-disclosure.

problem: "A first part that fixes a structure is reviewed before anyone can study what the later parts need of it" goes beyond ax:first-review, which limits only detailed study by reviewers, and only until the later parts are presented. The author can study them, and reviewers can once later-part papers are published.
fix: "is reviewed before reviewers can study in detail what later parts not yet presented need of it", here and in l:thm-first-part.

problem: By ax:prefer and d:design-bound, a sponsor's interests can depend on particular features, so a similar design on the same topic from authors with other affiliations can serve the same interests. The model then predicts the same votes on it as shared technical views do, so the comparison in inf:sa-tell-apart does not tell the two apart.
fix: Compare the same participants' Against shares on a sponsor's proposals while that sponsor pays them and after they move to a sponsor whose interests do not include those proposals.

problem: Writing later parts before the first part is reviewed costs authors work that the review can make them redo (ax:review-cost, ax:redesign-cost), so authors who seek only easier review also publish each part after the last is adopted. inf:pa-ease weighs only review cost, so the timing test does not tell the two explanations apart.
fix: Tell them apart by whether later parts already written or implemented before the first part's adoption were kept out of the mailings until after it.

problem: The direction group's charter includes "Providing an opinion on any specific proposal", including whether it should be pursued and what changes to consider, and design rooms are "strongly encouraged to give weight" to it (f:direction-opinion). That is a role of judging a design's quality, without power to rule, so "SD-4 assigns no one to judge a design's quality" and the matching words of f:no-merit-ruling are contradicted by the proof's own fact.
fix: "SD-4 assigns no one to rule on a design's quality, though the direction group gives opinions the design rooms are asked to weigh", with f:no-merit-ruling limited to ruling.

problem: The list leaves out that a user can vote where a national position is formed: INCITS counts "self-employed or self-financed individuals" as organizations with one voting membership each (f:incits-organization, f:incits-one-vote). l:settled-user and l:thm-pattern therefore test the user's choice against an incomplete set of moves.
fix: Add "or, where a national body's rules allow, vote as a member where its position is formed, as INCITS admits self-financed individuals", and weigh that move in l:settled-user.

problem: Every rule the sentence lists, the on-time paper, the presenter, a rival's need for a paper, and the forms and deadline for objections, is written in SD-4, which anyone can read and every participant is expected to know (f:familiar). ax:learning says only that how the committee works is partly learned by attending, so "some only that way" and the Theorem's "forms and times that attending teaches" go beyond it.
fix: "Participants learn how the committee applies these rules partly by attending, some of it only that way", here, in l:rules-by-attending, and in the Theorem.

problem: "Only through" rests on documents the proof has not searched: SD-4 says it does not repeat material on how to take part, who can join the committee email lists, and how to get initial feedback on an idea, and f:absences says the proof does not search those documents. The list also leaves out liaison organizations, whose representatives take part and act for them (f:experts-appointed, f:experts-personal). inf:thm-no-user-vote and the chapter's closing repeat the claim.
fix: "Within the documents searched, users' interests reach decisions through what participants value, papers a participant presents, TS feedback, national bodies, and liaison organizations", here and in inf:thm-no-user-vote.

problem: SD-4 asks a good paper to "Be example-based: Demonstrate motivating examples of how the code we have to write today is problematic and needs improvement" (SD-4, "Proposals and papers", not quoted in the proof). That ties each proposal to concrete code, a check on proposing for needs that do not match users' which neither this sentence nor p:checks states.
fix: Quote the example-based request and add it to l:checks-alternatives.

problem: A result-seeking author's gain "depends on how well the adopted design serves its users" (d:result-seeking), and ax:prefer has every participant value a good result for users, so a flaw found after adoption lowers authors' gain too. The Theorem's "An author gains at adoption, while a hidden flaw costs users later" implies authors bear none of that cost.
fix: "An author gains from adoption itself at adoption, and bears a hidden flaw's later cost only as far as they value a good result for users", here and in the Theorem.

problem: SD-4 says a TS or white paper "unblocks early implementers and users" (SD-4, "Technical Specifications (TS) and White Papers", not quoted in the proof), so a TS brings a design to implementers and users before the IS would. The sentence counts only the delay and the risk of change, and l:settled-design-bound and c:lever-ts-path rank the TS on that incomplete account.
fix: Quote that line and add that a TS also brings the design to implementers and users sooner than the IS.

problem: inf:user-price reasons that a user is not a participant and so bears the full price alone, but a user who decides to take part becomes a participant, and an employer or other sponsor can pay their costs (d:sponsor). The Theorem's "a cost borne alone" is false for any user whose employer would pay.
fix: "a user who would take part at their own expense bears the full price alone", here, in inf:user-price, and in the Theorem.

problem: "appeals are open" leaves out who may appeal. ISO gives the right of appeal only to national bodies and P-members (f:appeal, f:appeal-pmember), so no user or individual participant can appeal except through a national body.
fix: "national bodies can appeal", here and in l:checks-record.

problem: "review whose gain is spread across all users goes undone" drops the condition p:review-shortfall needs. Every design's gain is spread across its feature's users (ax:users-affected), and review is done whenever it is worth its cost to some participant, such as one with a large stake (l:skip-study, p:light-review), so as written the sentence says no review is done.
fix: "review worth more to users together than it costs, but less to any one participant, goes undone", here and in l:thm-gaps.

problem: "The rules also contain checks on each of these effects" is not shown. p:checks lists checks but never ties them to effects, and none of its items bears on a first part being adopted before reviewers can study what later parts require of it, or on review that is worth more to users together than to any one participant.
fix: "The rules also contain checks on several of these effects", or tie each check in p:checks to the effects it limits.

problem: Several predictions name evidence SD-4 keeps protected. The share of those present not voting needs the number present at each poll (inf:al-evidence), the sponsor prediction needs who was present and who paid them, and the written-answer comparison needs what chairs said at plenary, all held in meeting records and wikis, while f:protected lets only poll questions and numeric results be quoted.
fix: Say which evidence needs access to the protected records, or name a quotable substitute for each.

problem: SD-4 describes issues lists as holding minor wording issues that do not affect the design (f:no-paper), so many defect reports with few removals also fit the innocent explanation that adopted designs rarely need removal. inf:rm-tell-apart does not tell the two apart.
fix: Compare removals with reports or papers that themselves propose removing the feature.

problem: The two groups overlap. SD-4 says most plenary polls pass by unanimous consent, so a feature adopted by unanimous consent at plenary may still have drawn Against votes in its subgroups, and inf:de-predict does not say at which poll the Against votes are counted.
fix: Define both groups by the design room's forwarding poll: features forwarded while Against votes remained, against features forwarded with none.

problem: "national bodies ballot only on whole documents" leaves out the committee stage, where SC22's chair judges consensus among the P-members (f:pmember-consensus), sustained opposition applies because ISO excludes only enquiry and approval ballots (f:not-ballots), and "Consideration of successive committee drafts should be focused on resolving the comments raised by National Bodies and liaisons for the purpose of achieving consensus among the P-members" (ISO/IEC Directives Part 1, 2.5.6, not quoted in the proof). National bodies weigh in item by item before any whole-document ballot.
fix: Add "after a committee stage at which successive drafts focus on resolving national body comments", quoting that sentence of 2.5.6.

problem: The list leaves out two moves the proof's own facts give national bodies: forcing, with one other P-member, a meeting to discuss the SC22 chair's decision after an enquiry ballot (f:respond-comments), and confirming or declining to confirm the appointment of a convenor from its own country (f:convenor-term). l:settled-nb and l:thm-pattern therefore test the national body's choice against an incomplete set of moves.
fix: Add both moves to m:moves-nb and weigh them in l:settled-nb.

problem: The definition also requires "a process that involves seeking to take into account the views of all parties concerned and to reconcile any conflicting arguments" (f:consensus-def). An objection whose argument the process never sought to reconcile leaves that part unmet, so "prevents consensus only if" the three conditions hold is incomplete, and l:call-from-votes and the Theorem's merit sentence rest on it.
fix: "an objection prevents consensus as a sustained opposition only if", adding that the definition also requires a process that seeks to reconcile conflicting arguments.

problem: SD-4 calls a repeated ballot comment out of harmony with accepting group decisions only when it "comes from a national body that was present at the meeting and had an opportunity to have their objections be heard and considered" (f:ballot-decided). The sentence drops that condition, so it reaches national bodies that could not attend, and p:written-answer and l:settled-nb rely on it.
fix: Add "from a national body that was present when the matter was decided and had the opportunity to be heard".

problem: ISO lets a working group or subgroup decide on matters whose documents missed the distribution deadlines only if "the leadership shall ensure that all P-members or Experts present agree to proceed" (ISO/IEC Directives Part 1, 5.4, not quoted in the proof). On such matters one expert present can withhold that agreement, so an objection can count for more than a vote, a check this sentence and p:fluency leave out.
fix: Quote 5.4 and add "except that any expert present can withhold the agreement ISO requires before a decision on documents distributed late".

problem: SD-4 says "Any technical changes made during ballot comment resolution have one goal: to improve consensus" (SD-4, "Ballots and comments", not quoted in the proof). A removal a national body requests in a ballot comment is weighed by that goal, which the proof does not show needs the 2:1 norm in a design room, so this sentence and p:burden-flip's "a paper or ballot comment to remove it normally needs the same" are unsupported for comments.
fix: Limit the 2:1 claim to removal by paper, and add that a removal requested in a ballot comment is a change whose stated goal is to improve consensus.

problem: The 2:1 norm says when a proposal "normally advances"; it does not say a proposal advances only then, and SD-4 also says subgroup polls "should favor progress" (f:favor-progress). Declaring consensus at or below 2:1 lacks the norm's support but breaks no stated rule, so "departs from it" and the risk to the chair's post built on it are unsupported. The same reading of "normally advances if" as "only if" underlies l:norm-forwarding, p:cutoff-effect, p:burden-flip, l:removal-polls, l:sg-call, and l:settled-design-chair.
fix: "declaring consensus lacks the norm's support", resting the chair's risk at that count on that, and stating as an assumption, rather than deriving from the norm, that the chair forwards only above 2:1 in the items listed.

problem: SD-4 says a TS is balloted "with a round of formal review comments collated by ISO that must be formally responded to with a Disposition of Comments paper" (SD-4, "Technical Specifications (TS) and White Papers", not quoted in the proof). That rule also requires written answers to objections, and the "apart from" list leaves it out.
fix: Add "and the Disposition of Comments paper that answers a TS ballot's comments", quoting that line.

problem: A successful No does not cost a body the rest of the document. A failed enquiry draft can be revised and circulated again (ISO/IEC Directives Part 1, 2.6.4 c, not quoted in the proof), and a failed final draft can be resubmitted modified (f:failed-fdis), so a body valuing the rest weighs a delay to it against removing one feature. The ranking, t:nb-ballot, p:credible-threat, and l:settled-nb overstate what a No gives up.
fix: Define "values the rest" as valuing publication of the rest on schedule above removing the feature through a failed ballot and a revised draft, and quote 2.6.4 c.

problem: inf:no-gains-nothing says a No only lowers approval's chance, but ISO requires that "Every attempt shall be made to resolve negative votes" (f:respond-comments) and that a failed final draft be reconsidered "in light of the technical reasons submitted in support of the negative votes" (f:failed-fdis). A No with comments draws an obligation that a Yes with the same comments does not, whatever SD-4 says of WG21's practice.
fix: Limit the lemma to a body that expects the attempt to resolve its No to bring nothing beyond what its comments would bring under a Yes.

problem: INCITS also provides that "All official U.S. positions shall be supported by all U.S. delegates" and that the TAG "may determine official US positions on Plenary meeting agenda items in advance of the meeting, and the delegation shall abide by those positions" (INCITS Organization, Policies and Procedures, 7.17.1.3, not quoted in the proof). Where a United States position exists, this limits how a sponsor's paid United States delegates can weigh in, a check this sentence and l:incits-votes leave out.
fix: Quote 7.17.1.3 in f:incits and add both provisions to l:incits-votes.

problem: ISO requires the convenor to "act in a purely international capacity, divesting themselves of a national position" (f:wg-consensus). The proof quotes this but never applies it, though it limits the stakes a convenor may weigh against SD-4's plenary procedure, and p:checks leaves it out.
fix: Add f:wg-consensus to this lemma's basis and to p:checks as a limit on the convenor's stake.

problem: After a direction poll, the room directs changes the author is expected to make (f:direction-implement), so a like rival polled afterward faces an improved incumbent. Less support for it afterward fits the innocent explanation too, and inf:rp-tell-apart does not tell the two apart.
fix: Compare like rivals before and after incumbency only where the incumbent's content did not change between the polls.

problem: A national body need not form its positions in meeting hours: ISO asks national bodies to make their standpoint clear "at an early stage of the work" (f:iso-early), and INCITS lets the TAG set United States positions before the meeting (7.17.1.3, not quoted in the proof). The fixed hours of a meeting do not limit positions formed between meetings, so "few proposals" does not follow from ax:hours.
fix: Rest the step on the members' time a position takes wherever it is formed, not on the meeting's fixed hours.

problem: The prediction rests on what forming a position costs a national body (inf:nb-cost), but SD-4 notes that some national bodies "have included all comments from their members without vetting", yielding comments "that a majority of the national body's own members did not support" (SD-4, "Ballots and comments", not quoted in the proof). Ballot comments therefore include positions formed without that cost, so they do not show where positions were formed at it.
fix: Quote that note and limit the evidence to comments the national body vetted.

problem: l:settled-convenor gives cases in which SD-4's procedure has the convenor declare consensus; it does not show that the convenor declares consensus "only when" opposition holds no national position. SD-4 says only that the convenor "will usually ask" whether Against votes are national positions, not what follows from the answer, so "the room's count does not settle opposition that holds one" is unsupported, and inf:nm-changes and inf:nm-weight rest on it.
fix: "SD-4 names no step by which the room's count settles opposition that holds a national position"

problem: The whole-document ballot would not be national bodies' main check. Their committee draft comments, which successive drafts are to focus on resolving (ISO/IEC Directives Part 1, 2.5.6, not quoted in the proof), and the response every comment must get (f:respond-comments) do not depend on forming positions during meetings, and inf:nl-ballot shows only that the ballot vote is the move that counts directly toward stopping a document.
fix: "the ballot vote would be the move that counts directly toward stopping a document"
